chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the minimum of what menstruation may be, and he said: Its minimum is three days, and its maximum is ten.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: the Imam addressed in the narration
key_terms.أَدْنَى: the minimum limit or least amount
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation as a legal category in ritual purity rulings
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the minimum duration mentioned for menstruation
key_terms.عَشَرَةٌ: ten days, the maximum duration mentioned for menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum and maximum length of menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the minimum and maximum duration of menstruation. It establishes that the least duration of ḥayḍ is three days and its greatest duration is ten days, making it a foundational report in jurisprudential discussions of ritual purity.
